title: Wilds of Eldraine Commander: card flavor text

paragraphs.text: He weaves glamours as easily as breathing, his otherworldly beauty entrancing fae and mortal alike.
"Ho, Shaggyfoot! Lumpton, pick up those hooves! Edgewall by sundown or I'll sell the lot of you to a witch!"
"My story ends when I say so."
"The High Fae are capable of magics that would make even the great Gadwick himself seem little more than a clumsy apprentice." —Chulane, Teller of Tales
"Your season has ended. We are eternal."
"Give me just a moment. I need to grow us a new bridge."
"United, our roar will level mountains."
"I will protect the less fortunate. I will love bravely. I will face despair and fight on. As a Capashen, I can do no less."
"Let the deception of the gods yield to the pure light of day." —Brimaz, king of Oreskos
Metal is scarce, smiths are pricey, and plate mail is heavy.
The best presents are impossible to regift.
She reaches beyond the physical realm, touching the ideals from which all creatures draw their power.
The rifts reach into infinite time streams, bringing the divergent products of alternate pasts into the present.
"The realm of the gods opens before me!"
A blazing sun that never sets.
"The arc of my blade has carved a path of light for the peace that will follow."
Behind every general who leads from the front is a nervous mage with a spell at the ready.
"The first griffins were made by the gods to capture falling stars; they were given the keenest eyes and the swiftest wings, and sent to keep watch above the clouds." —*The Cosmogony*
"I have found the courage to face death—twice, if I must."
"There shall be a vast shout and then a vaster silence." —Oracle *en*-Vec
Ivold gasped in surprise. Either a very strange insect had crawled onto one of the lenses or he was seeing geists at last!
Even before Teferi heard Wrenn's call, a few Zhalfirins were roused from sleep by a strange, otherworldly song.
"Try to pretend like you understand what's important."
The throng flitted from castle to castle, leaving a trail of star-crossed love, damaging rumors, and missing heirlooms in their wake.
"The patterns of crossing ripples reveal the future to those who know how to read them."
It took the banning of temporal manipulation at Tolaria West to teach its students the value of time.
"I see their moral dilemmas. I see their raw courage. I see their self-sacrifice. I see our victory."
"We're on the fortieth floor, with one window, no balcony. No one could possibly get in." —Minosz, Orzhov chief of security
"Sometimes the hardest choice is between two wonders." —Gadwick, the Wizened
"Your proofs were a bit nontraditional, but effective nonetheless. Full marks."
"The bonders work with creatures that fly, slink, and burrow. Assume they know everything." —Jirina Kudro
The masks float downstream toward the Mirrorlake, where faces arise to wear them.
"You aren't invited."
"Virtue is virtue, whatever the heart that nurtures it." —Malacan, Vantress exile
Good riddance.
One glamer leads him far from home. The next washes away his memory that home was ever anywhere but at her side.
"You made it asymmetrical just to annoy me, didn't you?" —Imbraham, Quandrix dean
In the end, the lights fade, the land withers, and only the dead and vile remain.
"The end is justified in being mean. Or something like that."
"Welcome to the winning team."
The masks, like the ancient trees they're grown from, lend strength to the dryads.
Kill a gnarlid with your first blow, or it'll cheerfully show you how it's done.
The emotional echoes of dryad gatherings attract lost souls.
"The wise learn from successes as well as mistakes."
Pretty, valuable, and delicious—a boggart thief's trifecta.
"There are many kinds of duty, and mine is to see our world grow and endure."
"Control the Great Conduit? You might as well try to divert a river with your hands."
The arrival of spring's first flowers is a sacred occasion to Karametra's acolytes, who fill the Setessan woods with song in celebration.
"A blessing is not a gift. It is a duty."
"Not all paths are found on the forest floor."
Those who displease Oona soon learn the extent of the armies she commands.
He had heard rumors of the cities—the constant noise, the stagnant air, the tainted water—and he had no wish to learn if they were true.
Mischief is its own reward.
It started as a mere drop of water. The Magic Mirror crystallized it into much more.
An emblem of a secret guild, the Dimir insignia is seen only by its own members—and the doomed.
"What do you have that I cannot obtain?" —Mairsil, the Pretender
"What is mana but possibility, an idea not yet given form?" —Jhoira, master artificer
Lost to time is the artificer's art of trapping light from a distant star in a ring of purest gold.
It is the forest beyond the horizon, the mountain waiting to be climbed, the new land across the endless sea.
The continent of Murasa lies beneath a blanket of dense vegetation, its enormous branches tangled so thickly that some inhabitants never see the ground.
Without Ardenvale's loyalty, the realm would greedily devour itself.
When defeat is near and guidance is scarce, all eyes look in one direction.
Murky Otarian tides hide the forgotten treacheries of the Phyrexian war.
"It was a strange morning. When we awoke, we found our trees transformed. We didn't know whether to water them or polish them." —Pulan, Bant orchardist
The stronghold of Theros's light.
Protected by glamers and guile, Glen Elendra harbors the elusive Oona, queen of the fae.
On Otaria, peace and harmony are rare. Places that provide both are cherished.
On the continent of Tazeem, rushing waters plunge through narrow canyons into mist-cloaked lakes.
"When gods become apathetic, the people will worship anyone who answers their pleas." —Kiora
In the autumn, she casts her seeds across the streets below, and come spring, her children rise in service to the Conclave.
